title: AppleSkin – Hunger, Saturation and Food Value HUD
side: Client-side; also install on the server for exact saturation and exhaustion values
features: Food tooltips show how much hunger and saturation each item restores
Saturation drawn as an overlay on the hunger bar
Exhaustion progress shown on the HUD
Preview of hunger and saturation you will regain while holding food
Preview of the health you will regain while holding food
Hunger, saturation and exhaustion values in the F3 debug screen
Changes no game mechanics, it only shows what vanilla hides
Fabric and NeoForge builds for Minecraft 26.3
paragraphs: Minecraft tracks more about hunger than the ten drumsticks on screen. Every food also restores hidden saturation, and every action builds up exhaustion that drains it. AppleSkin puts those numbers where you can see them, without changing how any of it works.

Hover over a food item and the tooltip shows exactly how much hunger and saturation it gives back. Hold food in your hand and the HUD previews the result: the part of the hunger bar it will refill, the saturation it adds and the health you can expect to regenerate. Saturation itself is drawn as an overlay on the hunger bar, so you can tell when it is time to eat before your health stops regenerating.

AppleSkin runs on the client, but it needs to be on the server as well to show exact saturation and exhaustion values in multiplayer. It is one of the most downloaded Minecraft mods and fits into almost any modpack.

title: Mouse Tweaks – Faster Inventory Management with Mouse Drags and Scrolling
features: Improved right-click dragging that can place an item into the same slot several times
Left-click drag with an item picks up every matching stack you pass over
Shift plus left-click drag shift-clicks every matching stack in one sweep
Shift plus left-click drag without an item moves stacks into the other inventory
Scroll wheel moves items between inventories
Every tweak can be turned on or off in the config file
Purely client-side, works on any server
Fabric and NeoForge builds for Minecraft 26.3
paragraphs: Sorting chests is the part of Minecraft nobody signed up for. Mouse Tweaks speeds it up by giving the mouse buttons and the scroll wheel more to do, while staying close enough to vanilla that it feels natural within minutes.

Hold left-click with an item and drag across the inventory to collect every matching stack. Add Shift to the same drag and all of those stacks are shift-clicked into the other container in one movement. Without an item on the cursor, a Shift drag moves every stack you pass over. Right-click dragging is improved too, so you can drop several items into the same crafting slot just by passing over it again, and the scroll wheel moves items between inventories.

Mouse Tweaks has no server-side part, so it works in single player and on any multiplayer server. Each tweak can be switched off in the config file if you prefer the vanilla behaviour for some of them.

title: Dynamic FPS – Lower FPS and Volume When Minecraft Is in the Background
optional: Mod Menu and Cloth Config for the in-game settings screen
features: Detects whether the game window is active, hovered, unfocused or hidden
Separate frame rate limit for each window state
Separate volume for each state, including muting the game in the background
Toast notifications can be paused while you are away
Idle mode with a custom timeout
Battery mode for laptops and handhelds, with an optional battery indicator on the HUD
Fixes a vanilla bug that wastes CPU in the background
Stops rendering the world behind the resource loading screen
Fabric and NeoForge builds for Minecraft 26.3
paragraphs: Minecraft keeps rendering at full speed even when you alt-tab to a browser or leave it paused on another monitor. Dynamic FPS notices when the window is in the background, unfocused, hidden or idle, and drops the frame rate, the volume or both to the levels you choose.

Each state has its own settings, so the game can stay smooth while you hover over it, slow down when it loses focus and almost stop when it is minimised. A separate profile kicks in when a laptop or handheld runs on battery, and the battery level can be shown on the HUD. Switching back is instant, because the game keeps checking for input several times a second even at a low frame rate.

Dynamic FPS also fixes a vanilla bug that keeps background CPU use higher than necessary, and it stops drawing the world behind the resource loading overlay. Low-end PCs and laptops benefit most. Install Mod Menu and Cloth Config if you want the settings screen in game.

title: Falling Leaves – Leaf Particles Drifting from Trees
features: Leaf blocks drop small leaf particles that drift to the ground
Spawn rate adjustable for each type of leaf block
Conifers, jungle trees and shrubs stay quiet by default and can be switched on
Works with trees from other mods
Works with resource packs that change leaf textures
Purely client-side, no server install needed
Fabric build for Minecraft 26.3
paragraphs: Vanilla trees are completely still. Falling Leaves gives them a little life by letting leaf particles drift down from leaf blocks, which makes forests feel calmer and more natural.

The effect is fully configurable. You choose which leaf types drop leaves and how often, and the conifer spawn rate has its own slider. Spruce, pine, jungle trees and shrubs do not drop leaves by default, so if your spruce forest looks empty, raise the conifer rate in the settings. Modded trees and leaf resource packs are supported out of the box.
The mod runs entirely on the client, so you can use it on any server. It needs Fabric API and Cloth Config.
credit: Originally made by RandomMcSomethin, maintained by Fourmisain and BrekiTomasson
optional: Mod Menu to open the settings screen

title: Lootr – Per-Player Loot Chests So Nobody Misses Out
side: Required on both server and client
features: Every loot container gets a separate inventory for each player
Works with chests, trapped chests, barrels, shulker boxes and minecarts
Loot containers have their own look
Containers turn from gold to blue once you have opened them
No more racing other players to fresh structures
Encourages exploring existing structures instead of generating new chunks
Fabric and NeoForge builds for Minecraft 26.3
paragraphs: On a multiplayer server the first person to reach a dungeon takes everything, and everyone after finds an empty chest or someone's leftover junk. Lootr fixes that by giving every loot container a separate inventory for each player who opens it.

Any container with a loot table works this way: chests, trapped chests, barrels, shulker boxes and minecarts. Lootr containers look different from normal ones, and their colour changes from gold to blue once you have looted them, so you can see at a glance which structures still hold something for you.
Because players no longer need to rush to unexplored land, they tend to explore what is already generated, which keeps world size down. Lootr must be installed on both the server and every client.
credit: Made by noobanidus, with embeddedt and ZestyBlaze

title: Tom's Simple Storage – Vanilla-Style Storage Network with Crafting Terminal
side: Required on both server and client
optional: Recipe viewers JEI, REI and EMI are supported
features: Storage Terminal to search and take items from every connected chest
Crafting Terminal with a built-in crafting grid
Inventory Connector that links chests and barrels into one network
Wireless Terminal to reach your storage from a distance
Filtered connectors to control what goes where
Inventory Hopper and Open Crate for moving items
Uses the chests and barrels you already have
Fabric and NeoForge builds for Minecraft 26.3
paragraphs: Big storage mods ask you to rebuild everything around drives and power. Tom's Simple Storage goes the other way: it connects the chests and barrels you already have and lets you reach all of them from one terminal.

Place an Inventory Connector, link your containers to it and add a Storage Terminal. From there you can search the whole network and pull out exactly what you need. The Crafting Terminal adds a crafting grid that takes ingredients straight from storage, and the Wireless Terminal lets you browse it from across the base. Filtered connectors, the Inventory Hopper and the Open Crate handle the rest of the item movement.
It keeps a vanilla look, so it suits survival worlds that are not built around tech mods. The mod must be installed on the server and on every client.

title: RightClickHarvest – Harvest and Replant Crops with One Right Click
side: Required on the server, optional on the client
features: Right-click a grown crop to harvest it and replant the seed automatically
Works with all vanilla crops, including cocoa beans, cactus and sugar cane
Fortune on your hoe increases the yield
Works with almost all modded crops without extra setup
Optional rule that a hoe is required
Higher tier hoes can harvest in a larger radius
Harvesting can cost hunger or give or take XP if you want
Fabric and NeoForge builds for Minecraft 26.3
paragraphs: Vanilla farming means breaking every crop, picking up the drops and replanting by hand. RightClickHarvest turns that into a single right click: the crop is harvested and the seed goes straight back into the ground.

It handles every vanilla crop, from wheat and potatoes to cocoa beans, cactus and sugar cane, and almost all modded crops work without any configuration. Use a hoe with Fortune for bigger yields. With the radius option on, better hoes harvest a wider area in one go.
Server owners can make a hoe mandatory, charge hunger for each harvest, or reward or consume XP. The mod must be installed on the server; installing it on the client is optional.

title: Explosive Enhancement – Better Looking Explosions and Underwater Blasts
optional: YetAnotherConfigLib and Mod Menu for the settings screen
features: Reworked explosion animation with many new particles
Every new particle can be switched on or off
Special effect for explosions under water
Optional extra bubbles for underwater blasts
The whole mod can be disabled from its config
Purely visual, no change to explosion damage or range
Fabric build for Minecraft 26.3
paragraphs: A creeper explosion in vanilla is a quick grey puff. Explosive Enhancement replaces it with a fuller animation built from new particles, so TNT, creepers and every other blast finally look like they hit hard.

Each of the new particles can be turned on or off, which makes it easy to tune the effect for your PC or your taste. Explosions under water get their own effect, and you can add a burst of bubbles for an extra satisfying underwater blast.
The mod only changes how explosions look. Damage, range and block destruction stay vanilla, and nothing is needed on the server.
